sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1980. Queensland Canefields English of the late nineteenth century (A record of interview with two of the last surviving Kanakas in North Queensland, 1964). Pacific Linguistics D-29. Canberra: ANU. xiv+160 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-D29
sources.note: Section 4.1.1 Phonology (pp. 80-84) opens with an impressionistic remark that Tom Lammon's speech has 'a non-standard SAE rhythm' and 'a non-SAE placement of stress and... different intonation patterns' (p. 80); the rest of the section is segmental (consonant/vowel substitutions, epenthesis, deletion). p. 104 n. 2 explicitly discounts phonological variation 'e.g. stress placement' as inseparable from production factors. No rule of stress placement; texts are not stress-marked. Section 4.2.1 (p. 101, Peter Santo) is one sentence, no stress.
